clue.text: Abandon food, ultimately leading to hunger

indicators.note: leading to means the first piece goes in front of the next one
ultimately points to the final letter of the word food

parts.note: a hunger or craving for something is an itch

explanation.surface: Someone gives up eating, and in the end it only makes them hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the last letter of 'food', D, which goes in front of ITCH ('leading to').
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is to get rid of it or leave it behind, a synonym for abandon.

clue.text: Dad's upset — in despair unfortunately goes missing

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
unfortunately suggests the letters of despair have met a bad end and been jumbled
upset in a down answer means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: pa is a word for dad, plus the possessive s

explanation.surface: A father in a state of misery sadly vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns PAS into SAP, which goes 'in' DIPEARS, a rearrangement of DESPAIR ('unfortunately').
explanation.definitionFit: To disappear is to vanish, the same as going missing.

clue.text: Fox created endless fuss

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: A fox made a fuss that seemed to go on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the final O from TODO. 'created' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tod is an old and dialect word for a fox, still common in crosswords.

clue.text: Cross trashy bridge with bits falling off the sides

indicators.text: with bits falling off the sides
indicators.note: losing letters from both sides of the phrase trashy bridge leaves a run from inside it

explanation.surface: A badly built bridge is crumbling at its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an angry adjective or a verb for going over the bridge; it is a noun, a crossbreed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid is the offspring of two different breeds or varieties, so a cross.

clue.text: Old coins from this place chap quietly pocketed

indicators.note: something pocketed is held inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: hence in its old sense means from here
Alf is a common short man's name, a stock crossword chap
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A man here has slipped some antique coins into his pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: Halfpence were coins of old British money, before decimalisation in 1971; 'from this place' is the old sense of hence.
explanation.definitionFit: Halfpence were pre-decimal British coins, each worth half a penny, so they are old coins.

clue.text: With no end of pleasure, listen to girl's instrument

indicators.note: with no end means one end letter of the word is removed, here its first

parts.note: a charm is something that gives delight or pleasure

indicators.note: listen to signals that the name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Monica is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone takes no joy in hearing a young woman play music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no end of' cuts C from CHARM, giving HARM; 'listen to' then says HARM MONICA aloud, its two Ms running together into one sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica is a mouth organ, a small musical instrument blown and sucked.

clue.text: Composer's last bit of jazz featured in catalogue

indicators.note: featured in says one piece appears inside another

parts.note: a catalogue is a list

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: The final part of a jazz piece appears in a music catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last bit of' takes Z from 'jazz', which is 'featured in' LIST. The 's after 'Composer' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian composer and piano virtuoso of the 19th century.

clue.text: There's very little PM can somehow change ultimately

parts.note: William Pitt (father or son) was a British Prime Minister

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of can are rearranged in some way
ultimately points to the final letter of the word change

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister can barely alter anything in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges CAN into ANC; 'ultimately' gives E from 'change'. 'There's' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A pittance is a very small sum of money, so very little.

clue.text: No dinner set out for one without hotel room?

indicators.note: set out suggests things laid out afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: No meal is laid on for a guest who hasn't booked a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges NO DINNER SET. 'for' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-resident at a hotel is someone using its facilities without staying in a room there.

clue.text: Previous work put up in public display

parts.note: ex as a prefix means former or previous

indicators.note: put up in a down answer means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An earlier work of art is hung at an exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'put up' reads the piece upwards; 'in' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo is a large public exhibition, a display open to the public.

clue.text: Hair in buns dries out?

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about whether hair worn in buns dries out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of BUNS DRIES; the surface's hair in buns is a false picture, the answer being whiskers down the cheeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideburns are strips of hair grown down the sides of a man's face, so they are a kind of hair.

clue.text: So is fast rider not returning to London?

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word not is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
going to London is traditionally going up, whatever the direction

explanation.surface: A question whether a speedy rider is staying away from the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns NOT into TON. A ton-up rider is a motorcyclist doing over 100 mph; 'up' for travel to London is a British convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Ton-up describes a motorcyclist travelling at over a hundred miles an hour, so a fast rider is that.

clue.text: One place with tat — it could be this London street

indicators.note: could be says these letters might be rearranged into something else

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A place full of cheap junk, which might just be a particular London street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges ONE PLACE, TAT and IT together; 'with' only joins them. Petticoat Lane is a famous street market in east London, apt for tat.
explanation.definitionFit: Petticoat Lane is the popular name of Middlesex Street in east London, home to a well-known Sunday market.

clue.text: Political alliance — the first one Caesar was in

definitions.meaning: a ruling coalition of three men sharing power

definitions.text: the first one Caesar was in
definitions.meaning: Julius Caesar, Pompey and Crassus formed the First of these three-man ruling groups in ancient Rome

explanation.definitionFit: A triumvirate is a group of three sharing power; Caesar belonged to the First in 60 BC.

clue.text: Feels bad, then experiences rising morale

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of feels have gone wrong and are jumbled
rising in a down answer means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to meet with something is to experience it

explanation.surface: Someone feeling poorly finds their spirits lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges FEELS into SELFE; 'rising' turns MEETS into STEEM. 'then' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-esteem is confidence in one's own worth, close to personal morale.

clue.text: Ruler from East Russian commune

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east on a compass
a mir was a self-governing peasant commune in Tsarist Russia

explanation.surface: A leader who comes out of an eastern collective farm in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or prince, especially in the Middle East.

clue.text: Opposing charge, I have to be out for revenge

parts.note: v is short for versus, meaning against or opposing
to charge someone formally with a crime is to indict them
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A defendant facing a counter-charge vows to get even.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone vindictive is set on taking revenge, so they are out for revenge.

clue.text: Rescued, as Prometheus was bound to be?

definitions.text: as Prometheus was bound to be?
definitions.meaning: Prometheus, chained to a rock, had his liver eaten by an eagle each day, so read as ..., deprived of his liver

explanation.walkthrough: Prometheus Bound is the Greek tragedy; Heracles also freed him, so both senses fit him.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone is to save or free them; split up it also means losing a liver.

clue.text: Source of nearly all words of wisdom, I had gathered

indicators.note: gathered means one piece is gathered up inside another
nearly all means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a proverb is a short saying full of wisdom
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone collected almost every wise saying from one origin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'words of wisdom' is taken as a single saying; 'of' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A provider is one who supplies something, so a source of it.

clue.text: Extraordinary, like exam script having second scrutiny?

definitions.meaning: out of the ordinary, worth noticing

definitions.text: like exam script having second scrutiny?
definitions.meaning: read as ..., something that can be marked again, as a script is when it is reviewed

explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable means worthy of notice, out of the ordinary; split up it is also able to be marked again.

clue.text: Complaint in muscle

definitions.meaning: slang for a grievance or grumble

explanation.definitionFit: Beef is informal for a grievance, and it also means muscle or brawn, as in beefy.

clue.text: One's behind bore having noisy disagreement

indicators.note: noisy says the word for disagreement is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a breach is a rift or quarrel between parties

explanation.surface: A tedious person keeps getting into loud arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a dull person; it is the barrel of a gun, whose breech is at the back. 'having' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The breech is the rear part of a gun barrel, behind the bore.

clue.text: So, one who's had the sack will tell it how it is, maybe

definitions.text: So, one who's had the sack will tell it how it is, maybe

parts.words: So, one who's had the sack will tell it how it is, maybe
parts.note: sack is an old word for a dry white wine, so this is someone who has drunk wine and speaks the plain truth, not someone fired

explanation.surface: A worker just fired from their job feels free to speak bluntly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had the sack' looks like being dismissed; sack is a fortified wine of Shakespeare's day. The Latin tag means 'in wine is truth'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin proverb says that in wine there is truth: drinkers speak frankly.

clue.text: Magnificent head took position at front, not rear

parts.note: nob is slang for the head

indicators.note: not rear means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to have led is to have taken position at the front

explanation.surface: An impressive leader went to the front instead of the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took position at front' is a past-tense phrase, so the verb must be in the past too.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble can mean grand, stately or magnificent in appearance.

clue.text: Girl left on donkey

indicators.note: on in a down answer places the first piece on top of the second

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A young woman goes off riding a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places L on top of ASS in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lass is a Scottish and northern English word for a girl.

clue.text: Grant provided by an administrative district

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, giving a
a ward is an electoral or administrative division of a city

explanation.surface: Money handed out by a local council district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided by' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a sum granted, as a student grant is, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: What could be operable round front of gondola?

definitions.text: What could be operable round front of gondola?

indicators.note: round means the anagram goes around the next piece
could be says the letters of operable might be rearranged
the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A question about what equipment might work on a Venetian boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges OPERABLE into BAREPOLE, which goes 'round' G, the 'front of' gondola. The whole clue also describes the pole used to push a barge.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargepole is the long pole used to propel a barge, much as a gondola is punted along.

clue.text: I'm involved in row, and shout head off

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to roar is to shout loudly

explanation.surface: Someone caught up in a quarrel yells their head off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel; it is rowing a boat. 'head off' cuts R from ROAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An oar is the pole used in rowing, so it is involved in a row.

clue.text: Lead tip on manual weapon

indicators.note: on means one piece is placed after the other in this across answer

parts.note: a spear is a weapon thrown or thrust by hand
the head of something is its tip or point

explanation.surface: A metal point fitted onto a hand-held weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the metal or a dog's leash, but it is the verb, to head a campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: To spearhead a campaign is to lead it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: A lot of females hurry to get married

parts.note: to hare is to run or rush fast

explanation.surface: Lots of women rush off to wed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the women of a household in some traditional societies, so many women.
